 ALBEMARLE COUNTY, Va. (CBS19 NEWS) — Due to massive compliance issues, Albemarle County Public Schools announced on Wednesday that schools will close starting Thursday and stay closed through the Thanksgiving holiday.
 A source reports the division has found a “serious gap in its onboarding safeguards.”
 All new ACPS employees undergo a fingerprint-based criminal background check using the VSP criminal history database, but Virginia law and Albemarle County School Board policy also requires new hires to be checked against the Child Protective Services Central Registry.
 The problem behind this closure is associated with that registry.
 Students had been scheduled to be in classes for the rest of this week and on Monday and Tuesday next week before schools would close for Thanksgiving.
 The division has been roiled all year by a series of scandals, starting with two now-former staff members being arrested on sexual abuse and child porn charges.
 One of those staff members is accused of sexually abusing minors at the elementary school where he worked.
 That case is still pending in court.
 The child porn case is scheduled to wrap up in early December when the former staff member is sentenced.
 Following those arrests, former division Superintendent Dr. Matthew Haas was asked to resign, and Interim Superintendent Dr. Chandra Hayes was appointed to the post.
 Since then, three other current and former staff members have been arrested for failing to report suspected abuse.
 Additionally, two school board members have resigned, and another will step down next month.
 The Virginia Department of Education has also stepped in, ordering the division to conduct intensive reviews of policies and procedures.
 Below is a copy of a letter sent to ACPS staff members on Wednesday afternoon ahead of the public announcement:
 Dear Staff, 
 In a few minutes I will send a message to all ACPS families announcing the closure, but I wanted you to hear it from me first, so that you can begin to prepare. 
 We are closing because we discovered a serious gap in our onboarding safeguards. I know this news is alarming, and I understand the challenges many of our families and staff will face with such an unexpected closure. However, this is a necessary action to maintain the safety and trust of our students, families, and staff. 
 Immediate Issue Driving the Closure 
 Every new ACPS employee goes through a rigorous, fingerprint-based criminal background check using the State Police criminal history database. Virginia law and School Board policy also require that new hires be checked against the Child Protective Services Central Registry, which the Virginia Department of Social Services maintains, to confirm they have no founded complaints of child abuse or neglect. 
 During a review of onboarding procedures, we found that the criminal background checks were administered, but the personnel responsible for submissions to Child Protective Services did not consistently follow established processes. Specifically, over the past three years, more than 500 people hired by the division passed their criminal background checks, but their information was never submitted for the Social Services registry review. We investigated the matter and took immediate action. 
 Families should not have to accept any uncertainty about the adults working with their children, and I will not risk the safety of our students. Because the affected employees work in schools and departments across the entire division, I made the decision that we must close all schools until we have this issue resolved. We shared our findings with the Virginia Department of Education, and they agreed that staff who work directly with children must have their Social Services screening completed before working with students. 
 What we are doing now 
 We are working directly with the Virginia Department of Social Services (VDSS) to complete the screening as soon as possible. Staff who work directly with students are first in line, so that we can reopen schools quickly. VDSS has prioritized these submissions, and I am grateful for their support. 
 If your screening needs to be completed, Human Resources will contact you directly with instructions for submitting your consent form on Thursday. Please watch for that message and respond as quickly as possible. 
 If the VDSS review shows that any current employee is the subject of a founded complaint of child abuse or neglect, we will act immediately to protect students. School Board Policy GCDA requires that such an employee be dismissed once their appeal rights under state law have been exhausted, and it provides grounds for the division to recommend that the Virginia Board of Education revoke their teaching license. 
 We also checked whether anyone currently under investigation or facing charges related to abuse, neglect, or failure to report was among the employees not submitted. I can confirm that none of them were. 
 Schedule Through Thanksgiving Break 
 Thursday, Nov. 19 – Friday, Nov. 20: No school for students. All staff are expected to work as directed by their supervisor; these are teacher workdays for licensed staff. Staff may work from flexible locations consistent with our practice for normal teacher workdays. These days will provide teachers time to develop asynchronous learning opportunities for students to engage in on Friday and also to adjust their future lesson plans due to the sudden closure. 
 Monday, Nov. 23 – Tuesday, Nov. 24: The school division is closed. Staff will receive paid time off. Please take them to connect with family and friends. 
 Wednesday, Nov. 25 – Friday, Nov. 27: Thanksgiving break. Staff initially scheduled to work will receive paid time off.  
 Monday, Nov. 30: We hope to welcome students back. We will confirm the reopening by Friday, November 27. 
 Make-up days: We have enough instructional days built into the calendar and will not need to make up these days. If there are significant weather-related cancellations later in the school year, we will develop a plan at that time. 
 To those of you whose registry screening was not submitted: you did nothing wrong. You completed every step we asked of you. The gap was ours, not yours. Thank you for your patience as we make it right. 
 I also know the past several months have been hard. ACPS has been tarnished in the headlines more than any of us would like, and it is natural to feel that those stories reflect on each of us individually. But they do not tell the story of what happens in our classrooms, buses, cafeterias, and offices every day. The stories of our schools are the student who finally understands a lesson, the family greeted with kindness at the front office, the bus driver who knows every child by name. Your work is the reason ACPS is worth fixing, and it is why I am determined to stand with you and do the work necessary to fix it. 
 The changes we are making are not a judgment of our staff. They are about building systems worthy of our staff, so that the care and integrity you bring to your work every day are matched by the way this division operates. 
 Please use Monday and Tuesday to rest and be with the people who matter to you. When students return, they will need you at your best, and you deserve to have this time to step back and refresh.. 
 I am proud to serve alongside you, and I am grateful for everything you do for our students and families. 
 Sincerely, 
 Chandra Hayes, Ed.D. 
 Acting Superintendent 
 Albemarle County Public Schools

 And here is a copy of the letter Hayes sent to parents shortly after the division staff members were notified:
 Dear Albemarle County Public Schools Community, 
 When I took on this role, I made a commitment to you to look closely at how our school division operates, to fix what needs fixing, and to tell you what we find. Some of what follows is difficult to share, but you deserve to hear it directly from me. 
 Immediate Issue Driving the Closure 
 Every new ACPS employee goes through a rigorous, fingerprint-based criminal background check using the State Police criminal history database. Virginia law and School Board policy also require that new hires be checked against the Child Protective Services Central Registry, which the Virginia Department of Social Services (VDSS) maintains, to confirm they have no founded complaints of child abuse or neglect. 
 During a review of onboarding procedures, we found that the criminal background checks were administered, but the personnel responsible for submissions to Child Protective Services did not consistently follow established processes. Specifically, over the past three years, there were more than 500 people hired by the division who passed their criminal background checks, but their information was never submitted for the Social Services registry review. We investigated the matter and took immediate action. 
 Families should not have to accept any uncertainty about the adults working with their children, and I will not risk the safety of our students. Because the affected employees work in schools and departments across the entire division, I made the decision that we must close all schools until we have this issue resolved. We shared our findings with the Virginia Department of Education and they agreed that staff who work directly with children must have their Social Services screening complete before being able to work with students.  
 What we are doing now 
 We are working with the Virginia Department of Social Services (VDSS) to complete the screening as soon as possible. Staff who work directly with students will be first to be processed, so that we can reopen schools quickly. The VDSS has prioritized these submissions, and I am grateful for their support. 
 If the VDSS review shows that any current employee is the subject of a founded complaint of child abuse or neglect, we will act immediately to protect students. School Board Policy GCDA requires that such an employee be dismissed once their appeal rights under state law have been exhausted, and it provides grounds for the division to recommend that the Virginia Board of Education revoke their teaching license. 
 We also checked whether anyone currently under investigation or facing charges related to abuse, neglect, or failure to report was among the employees not submitted. I can confirm that none of them were. 
 What families need to know during the closure 
 Meals: school cafeterias will be open from 11:00 - 1:00 Thursday and Friday for regular lunch service.  
 Athletics and activities: You will hear directly from your school about any changes to the schedule. 
 Child care and before- and after-school programs: All before and after school child care programs are canceled. 
 Make-up days: We have enough instructional days included within the schedule and will not have to make up these days. If there are significant weather-related cancellations during the school year, we will develop a plan at that time as needed. 
 School Schedule Through Thanksgiving Break 
 Thursday, Nov. 19 – Friday, Nov. 20: No school for students. Teachers will provide asynchronous learning opportunities for students on Friday. All staff report as scheduled by their supervisor; these are teacher workdays for licensed staff.  
 Monday, Nov. 23 – Tuesday, Nov. 24: School division is closed. This includes all offices. 
 Wednesday, Nov. 25 – Friday, Nov. 27: Thanksgiving break, no school as scheduled. 
 Monday, Nov. 30: We hope to welcome students back. We will confirm the reopening by Friday, November 27. 
 Trust is built through honesty, especially when the news is hard. I’ll keep you informed as the checks are completed. I will receive a daily report from the Virginia Department of Social Services on the progress of the application review. This will allow me to confirm the reopening date by Nov. 27. With so little notice and the holiday season so close, I know this will be hard on many families, and I am sorry for that disruption. However, the safety of your children must always come first, and I believe this is a necessary action.  
 I will continue to review processes and procedures and make the changes needed to strengthen and restore Albemarle County Public Schools. Thank you for your continued support in those efforts.  
 Sincerely, 
 Chandra Hayes, Ed.D. 
 Acting Superintendent 
 Albemarle County Public Schools 
 The Albemarle County School Board will be holding a special meeting Wednesday at 7 p.m. It will be a closed-session meeting, which is not open to the public.
